# A tear-out's outer size has no runtime witness that it equals the tab body it replaced

## Context

#18532 named this invariant beside its own ("Related invariant, worth covering while the harness is open"): the popup a tab tears out into must have the **outer** size of the tab body it replaced, so neighbouring items are not overlapped — the content is legitimately smaller by the chrome. The #18532 witness ships without it: its stage resizes both vessels to a small rig width right after the pop-out (the display budget forces it), and the shared pop-out helper returns no tab-body rect, so the assertion was not a three-line addition. The ticket's own rule applies: not cheap, so its own ticket rather than silent omission.

## The Problem

`Neo.Main#resizeWindow` verifies the requested size against `outerWidth`/`outerHeight`, so the engine half is self-consistent. Nothing at runtime relates that outer size back to the tab body's rect at the moment of the tear-out. A regression that handed the body's rect to a content-sized call would pass every unit test that supplies the numbers, and the popup would come up one chrome short on screen.

## Fact corrected while building the arm (2026-10-03)

The engine sizes the vessel to the **tabs node** the pane leaves — header strip and body together (`HeaderActions#measureDockPaneRect` measures the tab container; `Main#windowOpen` then `resizeTo`s the OUTER frame to that rect under `useTotalHeight`). Measured on real chrome: node 425×635, body alone 425×599 (a 36 px header strip), popup outer 425×635, chrome 67 px. "Tab body" in the title and below reads as that footprint; the invariant and the arm hold against the node's rect, and the receipt records the body beside it.

## The Architectural Reality

- The tear-out path opens the vessel from the dragged tab's body rect (Workstation `VesselWorkspace`, the native vessel open in `NativeVesselTransaction`), and the window manager publishes both `innerRect` and `outerRect` per window (`manager/Window.mjs`, `outerRect = innerRect − chrome`).
- The sibling e2e specs (`WorkstationNativeTitlebarDragNL`, `WorkstationNativePopupOverPopupNL`) already pop panes out through the real header action with `viewport: null` on real chrome; `test/playwright/e2e/utils/workstationPopOut.mjs` is the shared choreography.
- The Brain-gated NL e2e set does not run in CI (`NEO_AGENTOS_RUNTIME_ROOT` unset there), so the receipt is a local real-chrome run, as for #18532.

## The Fix

One e2e arm, in the Workstation native spec whose rig already holds a real popup: read the tab body's bounding rect in the main window immediately before the pop-out, read the popup's `outerWidth`/`outerHeight` (OS) and `manager.Window`'s `outerRect` immediately after adoption and **before** any rig resize, assert equality within the platform tolerance. Extend `workstationPopOut.mjs` to return the pre-pop-out body rect so the arm does not re-derive it. Chrome is read from the real window, never supplied.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The arm asserts popup outer size == the tabs node's size (width and height) within tolerance, on real chrome, before any rig resize; the receipt records the body rect beside it.
- [ ] Mutation-proven: removing the engine's outer-size correction (`Main#windowOpen`'s `resizeTo` under `useTotalHeight`) turns the arm red on the size line with the frame one chrome taller, not on a collateral failure.
- [ ] The pop-out helper returns the node rect and the body rect it measured; no spec re-measures them.
- [ ] A headless run (chrome 0) skips the arm with a stated reason, as #18532's arm does.

## Out of Scope

The re-show footprint (#18532). Any change to `Main`'s resize route or to the tear-out sizing itself.

## Related

Sibling of #18532 (same harness, the other half of the operator-stated multi-window size contract). Decision Record impact: `none` — test coverage for existing behaviour.
